gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the scanner in these 'all-in-one' bundles is a separate USB 3.0 device that only works through desktop software (CrealityScan on Windows 10/11 64-bit or macOS: at least an 8th-gen i5 and 8 GB RAM, with an i7, an Nvidia or AMD GPU and 16 GB recommended), so the scan-to-print plan needs a capable computer between the scanner and the printer. Revopoint's MetroX goes further: its laser-mode GPU acceleration needs Windows with an NVIDIA RTX 3050 or better, and Revopoint's minimum PC for it has 32 GB RAM.
standout_why: I opened the two cited Creality pages (the scanner-combo collection and the K2 Plus combo page) and the top organic result (3dprintmates.com). Neither Creality page names a scanner spec, a computer requirement or the export step; they show prices and shipping only. 3dprintmates covers mesh repair before slicing (non-manifold edges, hole filling), matte spray for shiny or dark parts, and remodelling mechanical parts. On hardware it gives only frame rates ('Up to 105 fps with NVIDIA GPU'), with no minimum PC, OS, RAM or USB 3.0 requirement. ChatGPT's own answer says 'One machine handles both scanning and printing', which hides the computer the plan depends on.
decides: This confirms the advice to buy a separate scanner and printer, and adds a condition before any pick: the shopper needs a Windows 10/11 64-bit or macOS computer with a USB 3.0 port. For the Creality Otter, the minimum is an 8th-gen i5 with 8 GB RAM; for smooth use, 16 GB and a dedicated GPU on Windows or an M-series Mac. With only an older laptop or a phone, the Otter bundles at $1,598–$1,799 won't work as sold. A shopper with a modest PC should avoid the Revopoint MetroX, whose Windows minimum is 32 GB RAM and an RTX 3050 and whose GPU acceleration doesn't run on a Mac. The step after scanning is: export STL from CrealityScan, then slice and print.

findings.label: PC requirement, Windows
findings.value: Windows 10/11 (64-bit). Minimum: Intel i5 8th gen or newer, 8 GB RAM. Recommended: Intel i7 7th gen or newer, Nvidia or AMD graphics card, 16 GB RAM
findings.source_title: CR-Scan Otter 3D Scanner Review: Small to Large, Scan It, Make It (Creality forum, posted by CREALITY 2024-04-24)
findings.note: Posted by the CREALITY account. creality.com/products/cr-scan-otter returned 404, and the store.creality.com Otter page lists no requirements. A Creality Cloud page snippet showed the same figures, but I couldn't open the rendered page.

findings.label: PC requirement, macOS
findings.value: Minimum: macOS 10.15.7 or later, Intel i5 8th gen or newer, 8 GB RAM. Recommended: macOS 11.7.7 or later, Apple M1/M2/M3, 16 GB RAM
findings.source_title: CR-Scan Otter 3D Scanner Review: Small to Large, Scan It, Make It (Creality forum)
findings.note: Quoted from Creality's post. The post doesn't mention phone or tablet use.

findings.label: Connection
findings.value: USB 3.0 port, using the USB 3.0 data cable
findings.source_title: CR-Scan Otter 3D Scanner Review: Small to Large, Scan It, Make It (Creality forum)
findings.note: Quote: 'Connect to the computer's USB 3.0 port using the USB 3.0 data cable.' The post says a USB 2.0 power cable can be added if the port doesn't supply enough power.

findings.label: Scan-to-print step
findings.value: Export the model from CrealityScan as .STL, then upload it to Creality Print (the slicer)
findings.source_title: CR-Scan Otter 3D Scanner Review: Small to Large, Scan It, Make It (Creality forum)
findings.note: Quote: 'Export scanned models via CrealityScan in .STL format for direct upload to Creality Print.' The scanner doesn't talk to the printer directly.

findings.label: Object size range and accuracy
findings.value: 10–2,000 mm objects; up to 0.02 mm accuracy
findings.source_title: CR-Scan Otter 3D Scanner Review: Small to Large, Scan It, Make It (Creality forum)
findings.note: Maker's own claim. The post gives the range as 'Objects between 10-2000mm' in one place and '(10-2,000 m³)' in another, which looks like a unit typo.
